messages:
alex: Heads up — Support escalated from BrightHealth (tenant brighthealth) reporting sudden p95 regressions after last runtime deploy at ~08:40 UTC. Posting here to triage.

maria: Ticket number? cluster? any stack traces or 5xx spikes?

alex: Ticket #6021. Cluster: eu-central-1-prod-3. No consistent 5xx, but gateway 504s + high tail latency. p95 jumped ~6x (from ~85ms -> ~520ms). Traces show large KV/prefix cache miss rate increase.

sam: share grafana? curious about request types and sequence length.

alex: grafana.internal/d/qwe (redacted). Mostly short-chat traffic; sequence lengths unchanged. Metric `kv.prefix_cache.miss_rate` spiked from 1.8% -> 37% at 08:40.

liza: That smells like a sudden increase in prefix cardinality or a key normalization regression. Any recent PRs that touched request-key composition?

alex: Deploy at 08:39 pulled runtime PR that adjusted session header parsing (PR #8120). Might be related.

sanjay: I can repro in staging. Repro steps I used:
1) run `./tools/loadgen --tenants brighthealth --sessions 30k --concurrency 250`
2) set `PREFIX_CACHE_WARMUP=false` on the test runtime
3) send short chat requests for 15m
Result: miss_rate ~35% and p95 ~480ms.

jess: Immediate mitigations:
- Re-enable prefix cache warmup on canary nodes (warmup=true) to prefill base keys.
- Temporarily increase `prefix_cache.bucket_size` and `max_entries` for brighthealth in eu-central-1-prod-3.
- Patch ingress to normalize session tokens (replace with `<session>` placeholder) until PR is fixed.

liza: I inspected logs: we're seeing both `session:` and `session:0` and `session: ` (space) being emitted as suffixes. Intermittent parsing of X-Session header producing empty or whitespace ids.

```
[08:40:02] prefix_key=\"chat:brighthealth:session:\" cache_hit=false
[08:40:02] prefix_key=\"chat:brighthealth:session:0\" cache_hit=false
[08:40:03] prefix_key=\"chat:brighthealth:user:17\" cache_hit=true
```

sanjay: Quick hotfix idea: normalize at the parser layer — trim whitespace and map empty/zero-like values to `<session>`. I'll push a canary branch `hotfix/normalize-session-8120` and run canary restart on 2 nodes.

jess: Also add a short-term alert `kv.prefix_cardinality.tenants > 40k` to catch future spikes per tenant.

sam: After warmup on 2 canaries miss_rate dropped to ~10% in ~60s and p95 down to ~110ms. Good short-term.

opsbot: Runbook triggered: https://runbooks.internal/kv-cardinality-thrash. Oncall: sanjay, liza.

maria: I'll update the customer ticket: \"Investigating cache key normalization regression; mitigations applied (warmup + temporary cache increase). Hotfix PR planned; next update in 30m.\" Anything to add?

alex: Note PR #8120 touched header parsing for session, include that in the customer note.

sanjay: PR created and unit-tested: #8163 (normalize: trim -> map empty/zero -> `<session>`). Planning hot-restart of canary nodes in 20m. Will monitor `kv.prefix_normalized` log flag and `kv.prefix_cardinality_by_tenant` metric.

liza: Can we also add a structured log field `prefix_normalized=true/false` and a short sampling rate so we can search without noise?

jess: on it. I'll add `prefix_normalized` (boolean) and set sample rate to 1% by default, 100% when cardinality alert fires.

sam: Repro notes for postmortem: include loadgen script (`loadgen --sessions`) and the specific sequence of toggling warmup that reproduces the thrash. Save heap/profile for the runtime shard at the moment of spike.

maria: Action items recap — sanjay: merge + canary restart (ETA 2030m); liza: coordinate warmup rollout if canary good (ETA 3045m); jess: alert + logging changes (ETA 1h); sam: capture repro artifacts and attach to ticket (ETA 2h); maria: customer comms + postmortem stub (ETA 2h).

alex: Thanks team. Please post deploy status here. :thumbsup:
